name: Alchemy
long_description:
Alchemy is a nanotechnology company based in Kitchener, Ontario with core operations in the automotive and defense sectors. 

Automotive - With the widespread adoption of ADAS systems in new vehicles, the cost of replacing a windshield in new vehicles has tripled to $1500+. We have developed a windshield protection film product line called ExoShield to help vehicle owners protect their windshields. Our ExoShield GT3 film is sold through 400+ aftermarket installers and car dealerships in 56 countries that carry and install it for vehicle owners. For Jeep Wrangler and Ford Bronco owners (google: broken windshield club), our ExoShield ULTRA DIY kits are available via our website and dropshipping partners. 

Defense - Over the last 3 years, we have been working with the Canadian Armed Forces to develop an infrared camouflage technology. We have received two contracts from CAF to develop our technology. Our solution has the ability to be integrated into the uniform directly (adding just 5-10g of weight vs. 600-18,000 kg of weight for other alternatives), has outperformed all existing NATO alternatives in multiple CAF field trials, and is receiving support from major elements of CAF for our next contract. This technology can also be adapted for other individual camouflage integrations (face paint and individual nettings) and for mobile camouflage applications (vehicle nettings and vehicle paints).
one_liner: Nanotechnology-enabled coatings for automotive and defence sectors

name: Duranium
long_description:
China and Russia control the world’s critical minerals. We can produce Titanium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Zirconium & Hafnium in the U.S. more profitably than any existing process, and carbon neutrally via co-production.

Carbochlorination is the primary process for producing critical metals like titanium, hafnium, and zirconium, and was once the standard for magnesium. The problem: conventional carbochlorination relies on purchasing carbon feedstocks, wastes valuable byproducts, and is highly CO₂-intensive.

Duranium changes this with a novel reactor that recycles CO₂ emissions back into feedstock (CO) while generating a valuable co-product (bleaching agents). This closed loop slashes emissions and delivers Chinese-level metal pricing without subsidies — unlocking the full potential of carbochlorination for U.S. critical mineral production.

launches.title: Duranium — Reshoring critical metal production
launches.tagline: Reshoring critical light-weight metal production (Ti, Mg, Al, Zr, Hf) — more profitably than any other method through modernized carbochlorination and co-production.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93706&key=user_uploads/2509424/cab46185-5d50-4822-bf45-873f52ae6571)

**TL;DR** — **China and Russia control world’s critical minerals. We can produce Titanium, Magnesium, Aluminum, Zirconium & Hafnium in the U.S. more profitably than any existing process, and carbon neutrally. On track to supply 12% of U.S. magnesium by 2029, at 50%+ EBITDA margins (@ world’s lowest mkt prices).**

Hi all, we’re Berkley and Brenden of Duranium, and we’re delivering American critical mineral independence with a light-weight metal production process that competes globally without subsidies. As brothers-in-law, we’re passionate about rebuilding the U.S. industrial base — not through taxes and subsidies, but through real technological innovation. Our mission is to help America reclaim its place as the world’s greatest builder of _tangible_ things.

# ❌ The Problem

Magnesium, titanium, aluminum, hafnium, and zirconium are all listed on the DOE’s Critical Minerals List, with magnesium ranked among the highest in both supply risk and strategic importance to U.S. energy security. _The U.S. has zero domestic magnesium production and no titanium sponge production — yet both are indispensable for fighter jets, missiles, satellites, rockets, and advanced aerospace systems._ 

China and Russia control \~97% of magnesium and \~90% of titanium production (directly or indirectly). 

On top of that, U.S. magnesium costs nearly 3x the global average, and legacy methods are CO₂-intensive and waste valuable byproducts.

# ✨ Our Solution

We’ve modernized carbochlorination metallurgy (the primary methods for producing many of these critical metals) with a novel reactor and process that:

* Creates a closed-loop system that profitably matches Chinese pricing — without subsidies — and slashes emissions
* Recycles CO₂ emissions into CO feedstock
* Generates a valuable co-product (bleaching agents)

Others are trying to reinvent lightweight metal production from scratch with approaches that are costly and dependent on government subsidies or green premiums to hit profitability. Our approach is different: we harness the laws of thermodynamics instead of fighting them, co-producing valuable outputs that make the economics best-in-class.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93706&key=user_uploads/2509424/38fd63f0-e5a7-4f91-88cf-ad06c8b7e01a)

# 🏆 What we’ve achieved so far and where we’re headed

* We’ve proven the process at benchtop scale, producing magnesium, bleaching agents, and converting CO₂ produced by carbochlorination into CO
* We are now scaling with the build of a pilot facility to be operational by June 2026
* We’re on track to supply 12% of U.S. magnesium by 2029, at 50%+ EBITDA margins (@ world’s lowest mkt prices)

# 👥 Our Team

Berkley, CTO — A leading American expert in magnesium production; holds a patent for an electrochemical metal cell and built the _only_ U.S. pilot magnesium electrolyzer in the last 20+ years. Brings unmatched technical depth in lightweight metal production

Brenden, CEO — Former McKinsey D.C. consultant, where he advised the DoD on reshoring critical chemical production and spent 1 year with the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). Ex-Goldman TMT investment banker, Stanford Law graduate and Knight-Hennessy Scholar

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=93706&key=user_uploads/2509424/babe8628-8537-44c5-aa1a-daecb483c077)

## 🙏 Asks

Join our team! We’re looking for engineers with experience in high-temperature or corrosive reactors. If that’s you — or someone you know — and you want to help build the future of lightweight metal production, get in touch!

[team@duranium.co](mailto:team@duranium.co)

name: Kara
long_description:
Kara is building diamond semiconductors. 

We begin with growing ultra-high purity diamond wafers for advanced hardware. Used in data centers, spacecrafts, RF systems, and quantum hardware, our diamond moves heat up to 5× better than copper, helping critical systems run cooler, faster, and more reliably. 

Diamond has spent centuries as a symbol. We are turning it into infrastructure.

launches.title: Kara: Making Diamond an Engineering Material
launches.tagline: Kara grows and engineers diamond wafers for thermal management, semiconductor and quantum applications
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We grow high-purity diamond wafers for scientific and industrial applications. Our diamond thermal wafers can be used in aircraft, spacecraft, RF electronics, and lasers to move heat dramatically better than conventional materials. We’re helping hardware run cooler, faster, and more reliably with diamond that is 5× more thermally conductive than copper.

Here is a link to our launch video: 

<https://youtu.be/16aad1cU_FM>

**The Problem**

The world’s most valuable hardware systems are limited by how quickly they can remove heat.

For AI chips, that means expensive GPUs throttle and deliver less compute. In aircraft and satellites, it means carrying more cooling mass. In RF systems and lasers, it limits sustained output power.

Adding more cooling costs space, and energy, and sometimes is simply not possible.

**What We Built**

Diamond is usually something you wear. We make it something engineers can build with.

Diamond conducts heat up to **5× better than copper while weighing \~60% less** for the same volume. It is electrically insulating and stable in extreme environments.

Today we manufacture:

* Diamond heat spreaders for AI and high-performance computing
* Ultra-high-purity diamond wafers for thermal, photonic and quantum applications
* Diamond-metal composites (copper and aluminium) for thermal management
* Metallized and bondable diamond plates
* Custom-engineered diamond components

We are now producing custom samples under pilot agreements and purchase orders for thermal, electronic, aerospace, and quantum applications.

Silicon transformed computing when we learned to manufacture it with extreme purity and control. Kara is doing the same with diamond. Today, our ultra-high-purity diamond pulls heat away from silicon chips.

**Tomorrow, Kara’s control over purity and defects unlocks diamond as the ultimate semiconductor.**

**Why us**

[@Aarin Jhaveri](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669602) is a fifth-generation diamantaire who has sold millions of dollars in natural and lab-grown diamonds and worked across the supply chain.

[@Anuveer Chadha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669310) is a chemical engineer who has worked on diamond quantum sensing and advanced-materials research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with the Department of Defense and Department of Energy.

Diamond is our unfair advantage. We know how to grow, control, and engineer it far beyond jewelry.

**Our ask**

**Today, we're looking for introductions to engineers building hardware that is limited by heat.** 

Specifically:

* AI accelerator packaging teams
* Advanced packaging / OSAT engineers
* Aerospace, space, and defence electronics
* Data-centre infrastructure companies
* High-power RF and GaN teams

Introduce us to the engineer responsible for the hottest, hardest-to-cool hardware, especially where size, weight, or power makes cooling difficult. 

We’ll build them a custom diamond sample to test.

Email us at [founders@karalabs.ai](mailto:founders@karalabs.ai) or book time here: <https://calendly.com/aarin-berkeley/aarin-jhaveri-s-calender>

**Diamond spent centuries as a symbol of “extraordinary”. We are making it something the world can build with.**

launches.title: 83 Sciences: Materials discovery from the ~90% of experimental data that never gets published
launches.tagline: We train materials discovery models on experimental data to help industry improve manufacturing performance at scale and help academics publish more.
launches.body:
History’s greatest ages are named after materials (Stone Age, Bronze Age, Iron Age, Silicon Age, etc.). The next great age is ours to make together.\
\
<https://youtu.be/ysIdrc7mowM>
\
**TL;DR:** We are a team of Stanford, MIT, and Harvard researchers discovering breakthrough materials by training frontier models on decades of unpublished experimental data. **We've already discovered a novel material and drafted a manuscript for publication.**

Industrial R&D teams use us to find scalable application-specific materials that frontier models can't predict. Academic labs turn decades of unpublished data into new papers, citations, and commercialization revenue with us.

**What we do**

We are uncovering novel materials that help industry improve performance at scale and stay top of new regulations. Examples include replacements for PFAS, the "forever chemicals" that are being banned worldwide, and finding a binder for silicon anodes that can survive charging and drop into existing battery manufacturing processes (our cofounder Ian’s work at Sila Nanotechnologies).

**Why we're different**

The materials performance that matters to industry can only be measured in real experiments, but >85% of experimental research is never published. Frontier models train on papers and simulations and miss all the failures sitting in file drawers. We train on that unpublished data through partnerships with labs across the country, and it’s already working: we've already discovered a novel material and drafted a manuscript for publication.

**Who we are**

We are Eric, Ian, and Yankang, collaborators for years on everything from superconductors to cooling textiles, and we lead a team of world-class researchers and commercialization experts.

Eric developed one of the early generative AI approaches for analyzing experimental data (MIT PhD), Ian has brought multiple climate technologies to market, and Yankang led Boston Consulting Group’s AI program, scaling frontier technology to 30,000+ users globally. Advisors: Simon Billinge (UCSB), Mingda Li (MIT), Ashwin Sreenivas (Decagon).

**Our ask**

If you need better materials to drive performance and cost, especially in batteries, semis, membranes, catalysts or pharma, or know an academic lab sitting on experimental data, we'd love an intro: [hello@83sciences.ai](mailto:hello@83sciences.ai)

name: ChemPilot.ai
long_description:
ChemPilot accelerates the discovery and development of next generation defense materials using AI and data from our automated wet lab. Developing a new material today takes 10+ years of trial and error. We compress that to months by screening for what can actually be made, then closing the loop: every lab result feeds back into the models so the next round is faster and smarter.

Sam, Ofir and Maor spent two years researching these materials at the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana (former MIT postdoc), working directly with defense primes and government R&D agencies. Together we bring chemical engineering, computational chemistry and AI, plus the production systems to put them to work. ChemPilot spun out of that research.

The West’s defense and dual-use industrial base runs on materials with fragile, sole-source and often adversarial supply chains. Demand for new capability is surging, and materials still take decades to develop. We’re building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the materials the West needs, securely, fast and at cost.

launches.title: ChemPilot: Building an autonomous lab to discover the next generation of defense materials
launches.tagline: Building a new chemical company for the critical materials the West needs
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re Sam, Ofir and Maor, founders of ChemPilot (YC F26).

We are building a new kind of chemical prime: one that can autonomously discover, develop and ultimately manufacture the critical chemicals and materials the West needs. 

ChemPilot grew out of two and a half years of academic research by Sam and Ofir in the Technion lab of our CSO, Prof. Alon Grinberg Dana. During that research, we collaborated with a top defense prime and government R&D agencies to discover critical chemicals and materials using AI. We saw how urgently better materials were needed, and how slowly they were being developed.

Our models needed experimental data to predict what would work. That data was locked inside companies or had never been collected. Generating new data and testing candidates through defense primes and outsourced labs was too slow to support the pace of development we needed. We needed our own ability to generate high-quality experimental data at scale. That’s why we’re building an autonomous lab!

Maor joined the research effort a year ago, bringing his background in computer science and electrical engineering. Together, we began building the models, software and automation that would become ChemPilot.

<https://youtu.be/q5YMnXcxaIY?si=FkYf1ep25-kvI6vB>

Our AI agents research the chemistry, design new molecules and optimize formulations using predictive models and physics-based simulation, then build experimental protocols. Our lab makes and tests the candidates. Every result, failures included, feeds back into our models and informs the next experiment.

Our first lab is already running experiments, with robots working alongside our scientists. We’re automating it step by step toward full autonomy: AI deciding what to make next, and robots running experiments around the clock to produce consistent, traceable data at a scale we couldn’t imagine achieving manually.

We’re starting with polymers, coatings, resins and composites. Each program builds data and capabilities that help us develop the next product, growing a portfolio of high-performance materials on one platform. Our work on energetic materials and propellants is currently partnership-led, with plans to bring those capabilities into our own lab next.

Our future should be determined by how quickly we can invent and build, not what others are willing to supply.

Our asks:

* R&D and materials leaders at defense, aerospace or chemical companies: tell us the material you wish existed or optimized.
* Robotics and lab-automation builders: if you’ve built autonomous labs or robotic systems for chemistry and materials, we’d love to talk.

Reach us at [sam@chempilot.ai](mailto:sam@chempilot.ai).

launches.title: Primordiant: Programmable access to flexible scientific experimentation at scale
launches.tagline: On-demand experimentation in scientific data centers, run by self-evolving robot scientists, for the discoveries of tomorrow.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We're building general-purpose robot scientists that learn new tasks, adapt as experiments change, and improve on their own. We give people and AI agents **programmable access to physical experimentation at scale**, either in our labs or with our robots on-site in theirs. 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yd6z26toh6w>

**The problem**

AI models can now propose hypotheses and design experiments. Testing them still depends on human hands, or rigid lab automation scripted for custom machines that run inflexible scientific protocols. Discovery moves as fast as physical experimentation, and today those are slow, manual, and hard to scale. 

**Our solution**

Science needs experimentalists that **iterate as fast as a machine and adapt as readily as human scientists**. Primordiant's robots plan experiments, run them, observe what happens, and decide what to try next, closing the loop between reasoning and physical action . **Instead of building a new machine for every task, we're building generalist robot scientists that can take on whatever comes next**, and improve with every experiment. We’re firm believers in the Bitter Lesson, and we believe general purpose robots are the pathway to scaling scientific discovery.

**What we've built so far**

\- We designed and built our first robot in less than 3 weeks and took it to an early client's wet lab (They gave it a skull with goggles. We approve.) 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125694&key=user_uploads/2759626/82db9ca3-e7f1-421d-99d6-22b8cc3e57db)

\- We opened our own lab in Mountain View, where we're working with a second client to synthesize and test heat-resistant polymer coatings proposed by AI models.

\- A few weeks earlier, we ran our very first experiments from a makeshift materials lab in our Airbnb, in our pajamas :)\
\
**What comes next**: \*\*Scientific Data Centers!\*\*\
Compute became a utility once data centers let anyone use a server through an API. We think experimentation is next. We imagine **data-center-sized laboratories full of general-purpose robot scientists**, where anyone can call up a physical experiment as easily as a cloud GPU, and run it at a scale no human lab could match.\
\
**Team**

We are three Brown PhDs who have spent years building the core pieces: robots that act reliably in the real world, AI that does real science, and hands-on experimental physics. 

* [**Owen Tower**](https://linkedin.com/in/owen-tower-phd-270630133) **(PhD, Experimental Physics, Brown):** Studied topological phase transitions under Nobel Laureate Mike Kosterlitz, developing new algorithms and nanofluidic experiments for random-field Ising models. Ex **NASA JPL**, **CERN**.
* [**Cooper Niu**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cooper-niu) **(PhD, Theoretical Physics, Brown):** Created **ALBERT**, an AI particle physicist that **recovered the top quark's mass and properties from pre-1990 data in under an hour**. Ex **Fermilab**, **CERN**.
* [**Benedict Quartey**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/benedictquartey) **(PhD, Robotics, Brown):** Pioneer in **generally capable yet verifiable robot autonomy**. Created **LIMP** (ICRA 2025) one of the first systems that enabled robots to follow open-ended instructions with guarantees in the real-world. Ex **Boston Dynamics Robotics & AI Institute**.

\
**Our ask**\
If you lead R&D in **biotech, chemistry, materials, semiconductors** and want to run more experiments, faster, we'd love to put a robot scientist in your lab or run your experiments in ours. If you need high quality experimental data for scientific foundation models we would love to chat.\
\
How to get in touch:\
 📩[ founders@primordiant.com](mailto:founders@primordiant.com)

launches.title: Sinter: Accelerated Plastics Manufacturing
launches.tagline: The Fastest End-Use Plastic Parts in the World
launches.body:
Sinter accelerates plastics manufacturing with 48 hour injection molding production. Our additive tooling delivers end use plastics 10x faster and 10x cheaper than traditional methods, allowing teams to scale and iterate at previously unattainable rates for hardware development.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125314&key=user_uploads/3253127/79de7420-d976-4019-8cff-9f180f8c3c86)

We unlock these unit economics by building tooling with additive processes. Rather than using a traditional machined approach, our tooling is printed additively with photopolymer resin. They remain fully compatible with existing infrastructure while significantly lowering time and cost to manufacture, allowing even single digit part runs, something unheard of in the injection molding space.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125314&key=user_uploads/3253127/0d70c159-d98f-4ef0-9f9b-4af06e528c2b)

In our first month, we’ve helped companies produce over 500 kg of parts, seeing companies through first prototype to mass production tooling without forfeiting their ability to iterate.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125314&key=user_uploads/3253127/bfe5f102-3072-48ec-b115-229e7c1af6fc)

Justin and Oliver met online at 13 building custom formulated mechanical keyswitches to the tune of 5 figure months, and have been immersed in plastics manufacturing ever since. We both dropped out of college (before we got into YC!), and spent 4 months this summer living on the floor of an illegal, ant infested El Segundo warehouse to make Sinter come to life. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125314&key=user_uploads/3253127/2a77dfee-f2b6-41a4-abc8-cb9e58e60354)

Link to launch video here! <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dXiM2mVxXOQ>\
